commits.message:
fix(window): macOS compatibility for toast and taskbar flash

_flash_taskbar(): add early return on non-Windows — ctypes.windll
is Windows-only and the proxy Toplevel creation is pointless on macOS.

_send_toast(): replace unconditional PowerShell fallback with
platform-branched fallback:
  - Darwin  → osascript display notification (matches notifier/desktop.py)
  - Windows → PowerShell MessageBox (existing behaviour)
  - Linux   → silent (plyer already covers it if installed)

Also fix PowerShell single-quote escaping: use '' instead of \'
(PowerShell uses '' to escape inside single-quoted strings).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(window): suppress startup knock-knock and hide proxy off-screen

Two issues caused the window to quit during init with atm start:

1. First refresh marked ALL existing sessions as "newly alerting",
   triggering _knock() -> _flash_taskbar() which created a visible
   proxy Toplevel with a real close button.  Added _first_load flag:
   knock-knock is skipped on the initial populate.

2. Even with WM_DELETE_WINDOW bound, the proxy window appeared on
   screen (titlebar + taskbar entry).  Move it off-screen (-32000,-32000)
   so it is never visible to the user.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(window): bind WM_DELETE_WINDOW on flash proxy to prevent root destruction

The taskbar-flash proxy Toplevel had overrideredirect(False), giving it
a real title bar with an X button.  Without a WM_DELETE_WINDOW binding
Tkinter's default handler destroys the root window when the user clicks
it.  Bind the protocol to proxy.destroy so closing the proxy only
removes itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(daemon): don't use DETACHED_PROCESS for window on Windows

DETACHED_PROCESS strips the process's desktop access token, preventing
Tkinter from showing any window.  GUI daemons (window) only need
CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP to survive the shell; non-GUI daemons (watch)
keep DETACHED_PROCESS to avoid inheriting the parent console.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(window): exit process on X click instead of just destroying root window

root.destroy() closes the Tkinter window but leaves the Python process
running because the background refresh thread (daemon) keeps the
event loop alive.  Call sys.exit(0) after destroy so the process
terminates cleanly when the user closes the floating window.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(window): replace missing _stop_flash() call in _quit with inline cancel

_stop_flash() was referenced in _quit() but never defined, causing
AttributeError every refresh cycle and preventing the window from
closing cleanly.  Inline the cancel logic using the existing
_flash_after_id handle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(inference): keep ACTIVE when AI is waiting on internal process

Add RUNNING pattern category (en + zh) for phrases like "I'm running
tests", "please wait", "still in progress", etc.  These indicate the
AI is blocked on a subprocess/tool, not on the user.

Priority changes in infer_status():
  - New rule 4: RUNNING phrase in last AI msg → ACTIVE
  - Rule 5/6 (WAITING_USER): guarded by 5-min tool-call window;
    if a tool call happened within the last 5 min the session stays
    ACTIVE even if the AI's last message looks like a question.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(inference): move patterns to locale JSON files, zero CJK in .py source

Previously patterns.py contained Chinese characters directly in source,
making the codebase unwelcoming to international contributors.

New layout:
  inference/en.json    - English regex strings (compiled with re.IGNORECASE)
  inference/zh.json    - Chinese regex strings as Unicode escapes (\uXXXX),
                         compiled without flags
  inference/loader.py  - loads + compiles all locale files at import time;
                         cached after first call
  inference/patterns.py - now a 4-line shim, zero non-ASCII characters

Adding a new language requires only a new <xx>.json file and one line
in loader._LOCALES — no Python changes needed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(parsers): consolidate duplicate parse_ts() into base.py

6 parsers each had their own local timestamp-parsing function (_ts,
_parse_cursor_ts, etc.) with slight variations. Bugs or behaviour
changes had to be applied in multiple places.

- base.py: add shared parse_ts(value) that handles both Unix-ms ints
  and ISO-8601 strings with a UTC-aware result
- claude_code, cline, codex, continue_parser, copilot: remove local _ts(),
  import parse_ts from base, update all call sites
- cursor: remove _parse_cursor_ts staticmethod, use parse_ts throughout
- aider: unique _parse_ts(line) does regex on raw markdown; kept as-is
  since it has a fundamentally different input format

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(remote): register atexit cleanup for temp dirs to prevent accumulation

Each process run created a fresh temp dir via mkdtemp() that was never
removed. On long-running machines this accumulates dozens of stale
atm_remote_* directories. Register shutil.rmtree with atexit so each
temp dir is cleaned up when the process exits normally.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(main): replace N+1 DB queries with single batch query per refresh cycle

Previously _load_sessions() issued two separate SELECT queries per session:
one for the archive check and one for _merge_db_fields (user_label/priority).
With 10 sessions that's 20 sequential DB round-trips per refresh.

Changes:
- repository.py: add get_sessions_by_ids(ids) -> dict[str, Session] that
  fetches all rows in one SELECT ... WHERE id IN (...) query
- main.py: call get_sessions_by_ids once before the inference loop; use
  the resulting dict for both the ABANDONED filter and the label/priority merge
- Remove the now-unnecessary _merge_db_fields() helper function
- tests/test_age_filter.py: update monkeypatch target from the removed
  _merge_db_fields to get_sessions_by_ids

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(main): single parser instance per tool + remove unused ctx variables

- All 7 tool parsers in _load_sessions() were double-instantiated:
  one for discover() and a fresh one per parse() call. Now each tool
  creates exactly one parser instance and reuses it for all paths.
  This preserves any per-parser cached state (e.g. CursorParser._global_db).
- Remove two dead `ctx = typer.Context(app)` assignments in the `start`
  command foreground branch; the Context object was created and discarded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(notifier): escape quotes in PowerShell/AppleScript notification strings

Project names containing single quotes (e.g. "O'Brien") would break the
PowerShell string literal and cause a silent toast failure. Similarly,
double quotes in the macOS osascript path were unescaped.

- PowerShell: replace ' with '' before interpolation
- macOS: also escape " in osascript strings
- Simplify Darwin detection: use platform.system() == "Darwin" directly
  (hasattr(os, "uname") is always True on macOS and Linux alike)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(system): remove duplicate branch + dead if/else

- platform_utils.py: vscode_global_storage() had identical Windows and
  macOS branches; collapse to a single return via app_data() with Linux
  as the explicit exception
- daemon.py: stop() fallback had an if/else where both branches called
  os.kill(pid, SIGTERM); collapse to a single call

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cursor): eliminate instance-state bleed of n_prompts/n_gens across parse() calls

_last_n_prompts/_last_n_gens were stored as instance attributes, causing
values from workspace #N to leak into the ACTIVE-detection logic of
workspace #N+1 when the next DB had no prompts row.

Replace with local variables n_prompts/n_gens initialised to 0 at the
start of each parse() call and populated fresh from the current DB.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor: centralise MAX_MESSAGES + fix deprecated datetime.utcnow

- parsers/base.py: add MAX_MESSAGES = 40 constant (single source of truth)
- All 7 parsers: import MAX_MESSAGES from base, remove local _MAX_MESSAGES = 40
- store/models.py: replace datetime.utcnow (deprecated, naive) with
  _utcnow() -> datetime.now(timezone.utc) for all three model defaults

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(cursor): read full AI response text from globalStorage cursorDiskKV

Cursor stores actual conversation content (bubbles) in:
  %APPDATA%/Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb  (cursorDiskKV table)
with keys like bubbleId:<composerId>:<bubbleId>.

Previously the parser only read aiService.prompts (user text) and
aiService.generations.textDescription (a one-line summary), so the
full AI response was never captured.

New approach:
1. Read composer.composerData for composerIds (most-recent-first)
2. Query globalStorage cursorDiskKV for all bubbles matching those IDs
3. type 1 = user, type 2 = AI; sort by createdAt; build full conversation
4. Fall back to legacy chat-blob / prompts+generations paths when
   globalStorage is unavailable (SSH remote, older Cursor versions)

Also add global_db constructor param for test injection, update fixture
to create a synthetic globalStorage DB, and add test_parse_bubbles_full_ai_text.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cursor): detect ACTIVE state via prompt/gen count and db mtime

- Synthesize 'cursor:processing' ToolCall when prompts outnumber
  generations (unanswered prompt in flight) OR db mtime is fresher
  than the last generation timestamp by <60s
- Store _last_n_prompts/_last_n_gens on the parser instance so the
  in-flight signal survives past the parse() call
- Always use db_mtime as last_active for reliable freshness ordering
- Add two new tests: unmatched prompt makes user the last message,
  and active tool call emitted when db is newer than last generation

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(window): acknowledge alert by clicking the session card

Before: badge could only be cleared by clicking the red number itself
        (which zeroed everything at once).

Now: clicking any card in WAITING_USER / BLOCKED / COMPLETED state
     decrements the badge by 1 for that specific session, marking it
     as acknowledged. The user naturally looks at the card → one click
     = "I've seen this", badge goes down.

Implementation:
- SessionCard.__init__ accepts on_acknowledge callback
- Binds <Button-1> to on_acknowledge only when session.status is in
  _ACK_STATUSES (WAITING_USER / BLOCKED / COMPLETED)
- FloatingWidget._cmd_acknowledge: adds session.id to _badge_ack set,
  decrements _badge_count, re-renders badge
- Double-click still opens Inspect (existing behavior unchanged)
- Clicking the red badge number still clears all remaining alerts at once
  (useful as a "dismiss all" shortcut)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: filter empty sessions; fix cursor_proj name; skip UUID task desc

1. main.py — filter empty sessions before age check:
   Drop any session where total_turns==0 AND last_active is None AND
   last_ai_message is empty. These carry no information and clutter
   the view (e.g. Cursor workspace stubs with no conversation).

2. syncer.py (_sync_cursor_projects) — correct project_name:
   The parser was run against the local temp path, so project_name
   came out as a UUID fragment ("af0270d9/e2c51ce63aa9").
   Now overrides session.project_name using _project_name(pattr.filename),
   which decodes the remote workspace-path-encoded directory name the
   same way ClaudeCodeParser does for Claude Code sessions.

3. rules.py (infer_task_description) — skip UUID fallback:
   The final fallback "return session.project_name" was surfacing raw
   UUID/hash strings (e.g. "a453/e2c51ce63aa9") as the task description.
   Now checks if project_name looks like a UUID/hash (hex + dashes, 8+
   chars) and returns "" instead, so the card shows nothing rather than
   a meaningless identifier.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(window): replace continuous header flash with one-shot pulse

The continuous flash loop ran forever whenever any WAITING_USER session
existed, causing constant header flickering even for idle sessions
(since the new inference marks all 'AI spoke last' as WAITING_USER).

Changes:
- Remove _start_flash / _flash_tick / _stop_flash (continuous loop)
- Remove _alert_on flag (no longer needed)
- Add _flash_header_once(color, times=3): fires N on/off pulses then
  restores the header to normal — triggered once per new alert, not
  per refresh cycle
- _knock() chooses flash color by status: yellow=WAITING, red=BLOCKED,
  green=COMPLETED
- Header is now always static unless a new knock-knock fires

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(window): red badge counter on bell — auto +1/-1, click to dismiss

Header now shows a red circular badge next to the 🔔 bell:

  +1  when any session transitions into WAITING_USER / BLOCKED / COMPLETED
  -1  automatically when that session goes back to ACTIVE (user resumed)
  ×   click the badge to manually dismiss all pending alerts (zero it out)
  hidden when count == 0

Implementation:
- _badge_count: int tracks unacknowledged alert transitions
- _badge_ack: set tracks sessions the user has manually dismissed
- _render_badge(): toggles badge_bg oval + badge_num text visibility
- _dismiss_badge(): resets count to 0, marks current alert set as acked
- Badge oval has hover color (red→maroon) and cursor feedback
- Sessions that disappear entirely also decrement the counter
- Bell icon still appears/disappears independently of badge count

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(inference): detect AI-done-waiting state; expand COMPLETED patterns

Root cause: infer_status() returned ACTIVE for any session with a tool
call in the last 5 minutes, so sessions that finished their work and
were waiting for the next user instruction always showed RUN.

Changes to rules.py:
- _ACTIVE_WINDOW_SECONDS 300→60: only flag ACTIVE when a tool call
  happened in the last 60 s (i.e. the AI is actively running)
- New _last_turn_is_ai(): inspects message list to find whose turn it is
- New priority step 5: if AI spoke last AND session has ≥1 turn →
  WAITING_USER (the ball is in the user's court, regardless of last-msg text)
- Priority order now: ACTIVE(tool) → BLOCKED → COMPLETED → WAITING(pattern)
  → WAITING(structural/ai-spoke-last) → IDLE → LLM → ACTIVE

Changes to patterns.py (COMPLETED_PATTERNS):
- "I've completed/finished/implemented…"
- "The changes have been made/committed/pushed"
- "I've made the (requested|necessary) changes"
- "Let me know if there's anything else…" (common Claude sign-off)
- "You can now test/run/use…"
- "Is there anything else…" / "Anything else I can help with?"
- "The tests pass"
- Chinese equivalents for all of the above

New tests (4 added):
- test_waiting_user_when_ai_spoke_last
- test_active_when_user_spoke_last
- test_completed_by_let_me_know_pattern
- test_completed_by_you_can_now_pattern

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: age badge sync + knock-knock alerts for WAITING/BLOCKED/COMPLETED

Bug 1 — footer badge always showed "3d" even with --since 24:
- FloatingWidget now accepts initial_age_hours param
- Matches it to the closest _AGE_PRESETS entry (or inserts a custom one)
- Widget-level age filter uses min(widget_hours, external_hours) so the
  two filters never fight; badge always reflects the active limit
- main.py window() passes since= through to FloatingWidget

Bug 2 — no knock-knock when sessions need attention:
- _update_alert() now tracks per-session alert state (set of IDs)
  and fires on *status transition* into WAITING_USER / BLOCKED / COMPLETED
  (not just "count > 0"), so repeated refreshes don't re-alert
- COMPLETED added to alert set alongside WAITING_USER and BLOCKED
- _knock() fires toast + taskbar flash for each newly-alerting session
- _send_toast() tries plyer first, falls back to PowerShell MessageBox
- _flash_taskbar() fixed: overrideredirect windows have no taskbar HWND,
  so a tiny invisible proxy Toplevel is created, flashed (6 times), then
  destroyed after 3s — this makes the taskbar button actually blink

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(window): show latest AI output on each session card

Card layout extended from 3 rows to 4 (CARD_H 76→90):

  row 2  task description (dim) · status badge · priority
  row 3  latest AI message — the actual model output
  row 4  progress bar · % · ⚠ needs-you nudge

Added _clean_ai_msg() to strip noise before display:
  - removes <tool_use>…</tool_use> and other XML tag blocks
  - strips fenced code blocks (```…```)
  - collapses multi-line output to a single preview line
  - truncates to 44 chars with ellipsis

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: daemon start/stop/restart/ps/log CLI commands

Add background process management for the floating window and terminal
TUI so they can run unattended and be controlled from any shell.

New commands:
  atm start [window|watch]   launch as detached background process
  atm stop  [window|watch]   terminate the daemon gracefully
  atm restart [window|watch] stop + start (picks up new config)
  atm ps                     show running daemons with PID + log path
  atm log [window|watch]     tail the daemon's log file

Implementation (system/daemon.py):
- PID files at ~/.config/aitaskmonitor/<name>.pid
- Log files at ~/.config/aitaskmonitor/<name>.log
- Windows: DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP so the daemon
  survives terminal close
- POSIX: start_new_session=True for the same effect
- psutil used for reliable liveness check; falls back to os.kill(pid, 0)
- Stale PID files auto-cleaned on next status check
- All commands default to 'window' mode for zero-argument convenience:
    atm start     # starts the floating window in background
    atm stop      # stops it
    atm restart   # picks up config changes
- --fg flag on `atm start` for foreground (debugging)
